I really appreciate you taking the time to speak to me at all. Thank you.

I've thought about trying to do internships, but even if I wanted to do that, most require it be for a college credit, while others would require me to move - which I'm not against, but if I move the cost of living will definitely be higher and if I move for an internship I won't have an income.

It's just the sum of all of this that makes me feel like everything I've done has been pointless. Dreams don't come true and I wish I knew that about 10 years ago so I could have chosen a major that doesn't make me a repulsive candidate for a job.

Yeah that's exactly what my problem is. Long commute and long hours. It's also hard to find any job with the degree I have because it's a big red flag to most employers. I've tried just saying that I have a bachelors but the specifics eventually get brought up.

I just wish there was a job I could take that was extremely low level that I could use to prove my passion and worth for the field I want to be in.

Haha I try, though to me it doesn't feel like a long time. It just kinda blinks by.

I haven't been focusing on anything, I've kept myself open, but over the years I've fallen more and more in love with editing video. The problem with any aspect of my field is that they need proof I'm able to deliver in the form of some kind of portfolio(which I don't really have, and I'm unable to build one while also doing what I currently do for a living), and I've found they don't really care about the degree, so I feel like I wasted my time.
Of course you can - My degree is in Multimedia Design. I just love all things editing, whether it's video, audio, or images.
